themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: The memory selloff deepened. Micron closed down 3.88% at $989.04 on Oct 12 and every stock in the SOX fell; on Oct 13 Korea's KOSPI fell about 6% below 6,000 with SK Hynix about -8.5% and Samsung about -6.8%, and Kioxia fell 13% in Tokyo. CXMT says it will launch DDR5 server memory on a denser 4F2 design around the end of 2026. Optics were sold too: Lumentum -9.8% and Coherent -7.9% on Oct 12, on profit taking rather than any demand news.
themes.for_you: Skip memory swings. ANET (swing setup) is 3.3% under its 217.85 pivot; wait for TSMC on Thursday. COHR is Buy zone now at the bottom of its zone but falling, so a small first tranche at most. LRCX and AMAT are left out of the bearish list because tool orders lag; watch what TSMC says about 2027 capex.

themes.name: AI power and the grid
themes.what: The Energy Department offered Vistra a conditional loan of up to $4.2 billion (announced Oct 5) for uprates and upgrades at Beaver Valley, Davis-Besse and Perry. The work adds 433 MW, keeps nearly 4 GW of nuclear online for 20 more years and backs a 2.6 GW power deal with Meta. Cheap federal money for uprates lowers the cost of new nuclear output for data centers.
themes.for_you: No action. VST is rated Avoid on the dashboard, so this is not a buy signal. It confirms the theme: existing nuclear plants are the fastest new power for AI. The loan is conditional, not signed.

themes.name: Fintech and Crypto Rails: Stablecoins, Tokenization, Exchanges
themes.what: Bank results split on Oct 13: JPMorgan missed on earnings ($5.57 vs $5.93) and revenue ($50.17B vs $51.23B) as expenses rose 12%, while Citi beat ($2.85 vs $2.62, revenue up 8%). Separately, Morgan Stanley pushed its tokenized stock trading target to Q1 2027 from the second half of 2026, saying market plumbing and rules need more time.
themes.for_you: C beat and is Buy zone now: new put idea at $122 (see Setups). Do not buy JPM today; its one month drop could trip the chart check. MS is left out of both lists: the tokenization delay is a small setback for the theme, and MS reports Wednesday.

themes.name: Healthcare and Medtech: Aging, Heart, Sugar, Hearing, Sight
themes.what: UnitedHealth beat and raised 2026 adjusted EPS to at least $20.50 as its medical care ratio fell to 88.4% from 89.9% a year ago. J&J raised 2026 sales guidance to about $101.2 billion and adjusted EPS to $11.10 at the midpoints, with a talc settlement charge cutting GAAP EPS to $0.09. Medtronic rose 3.9% on 2.3x normal volume Oct 12 after its oversubscribed MiniMed swap.
themes.for_you: MDT is Buy zone now and its chart just got stronger; tranches fit. JNJ is rated Wait. ISRG is left out of both lists: a lower care ratio can mean insurers push back on procedures, but there is no sign of that yet; watch its report.

themes.name: Robotics, Automation and Physical AI
themes.what: XPeng set a timeline for its IRON humanoid at its Oct 12 Paris event: mass production by the end of 2026, deliveries in the first half of 2027, starting in stores and malls, and Europe later in 2027. Separately, a Wall Street Journal report says Walmart is still struggling to automate its US warehouses and that Symbotic does not expect a workable in store model until 2028.
themes.for_you: No action. SYM is in a downtrend and not a setup, even though ARK added a small amount Oct 12. XPEV is left out of both lists: a timeline is not orders. ZBRA, the robotics swing setup, is not affected.

innovations.name: Financials
innovations.what: Morgan Stanley moved its target for tokenized stock trading on its alternative trading system to Q1 2027 from the second half of 2026 (said Oct 12 at TOKEN2049), citing market plumbing, products and rules that still need time. It still sees tokenized real world assets reaching $3 to $10 trillion by 2030, against about $39 to $40 billion today.
innovations.for_you: No action. A big bank slipping its date is a reminder that tokenized stocks are years from mattering to earnings. MS is not on the dashboard lists; it reports Wednesday.

innovations.name: Industrials
innovations.what: Symbotic announced on Oct 13 that it is buying cellumation, a Bremen sortation company whose software driven floor replaces fixed conveyors. At the same time a Wall Street Journal report says Walmart's warehouse automation keeps hitting breakdowns and that Symbotic does not expect a workable in store pickup model until 2028, which pushes out the 400 store option.
innovations.for_you: No action. SYM is in a downtrend and the Walmart option is later than hoped; ZBRA (swing setup, entry 391.59, needs 959K+ shares) sells into the same warehouses but is not tied to Walmart's timeline.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.what: AtlasIntel's runoff poll for Bloomberg (Oct 3 to 8, 5,026 people, released Oct 9) gives Flavio Bolsonaro 52.8% of valid votes to Lula's 47.2%, wider than Datafolha's 52% to 48%. Bolsonaro rose from 47.4% to 51.1% of total votes since Atlas's last poll, breaking the earlier tie.
countries.for_you: Markets already price a Bolsonaro win, so the poll mostly lowers the odds of a shock. Still no new Brazil swings or puts into the Oct 25 runoff. PBR is left out of both lists: a new government could change its pricing policy either way.

countries.name: European Union
countries.what: European stocks held up through the global chip selloff. The Stoxx 600 closed up 0.65% at 635.65 on Oct 12 and rose about 0.6% to a one week high early Oct 13, led by banks and energy, because Europe owns few AI chip giants. Disappointing LVMH results weighed on luxury. ASML reports later this week.
countries.for_you: No action. ASML is left out of both lists until it reports; memory makers are big buyers of its tools, so its outlook matters for LRCX and AMAT too.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: UKMTO reported a crude tanker hit by an unknown projectile while leaving Hormuz on Oct 11 and a product tanker hit on Oct 12, and the IRGC claimed more tanker strikes. Brent settled at $106.65 on Oct 12. Saudi stocks steadied, with the TASI up 0.33% on Oct 13.
countries.for_you: XOM is 0.4% from its 172.91 pivot but needs 20.4M+ shares on the breakout day; COP (new setup) needs 10M+ over 141.91. FRO is left out: tanker rates rise but so do the risks to its ships.

countries.name: India
countries.what: India's 10 year bond yield rose to 7.37% on Oct 12, its highest since October 2023, even as the rupee bounced about 1% to near 95.76 per dollar on the RBI's new curbs. Bloomberg called the curbs among the strongest currency defenses since the 2013 taper tantrum.
countries.for_you: No action. Indian bank ADRs face higher funding costs and bond losses. INFY is left out of both lists: a weak rupee helps it, but the rupee just bounced.

countries.name: Japan
countries.what: Japan reopened after a holiday into the chip selloff. The Nikkei fell about 1.7% to 1.8% on Oct 13 as Kioxia dropped 13% and Tokyo Electron 7%, while the broader Topix rose about 0.1%. The damage was in chip stocks, not the whole market.
countries.for_you: No action. Kioxia and Tokyo Electron do not trade in the US. Exporters like TM and SONY were not part of the selling, so they are left out of both lists. The BOJ meets Oct 30.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.what: The peso rebounded 0.73% to about 18.26 per dollar on Oct 12 after last week's slide to its weakest since November 2025. September inflation rose to 3.45% a year from 3.26%, a bit under the 3.47% forecast. Banxico's next decision is Nov 5 at 6.50%.
countries.for_you: No action. One day's bounce does not change the trend; none of these names is on your setup lists. Airports (ASR, PAC) and KOF are left out of both lists because the move was small.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: The KOSPI fell about 6% on Oct 13, below 6,000 for the first time since August, and a sell sidecar paused program selling. SK Hynix fell about 8.5% and Samsung about 6.8%, with SK Square down about 12%.
countries.for_you: No action except to stay out. EWY fell 4% Monday and has more to digest; MU is not a setup. Watch the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.what: The Taiex fell 1.95% to 48,341 on Oct 13 as foreign investors sold a net NT$165 billion, the third largest foreign sale on record, after the US chip selloff and Korea's crash. TSMC fell 1.97% to NT$2,490 two days before its results.
countries.for_you: EWT dropped off the Setups list; no swing until after TSMC reports. The call is 2:00pm Taipei time Thursday, which is 2:00am ET. TSM is left out of the bearish list because its sales are still up over 50%; this is foreign money leaving, not a business change.
